headline: A SUNDAY WITHOUT A SINGLE SWING
subhead: Not one iron ball flew in Gasket, and the sheriff has not stopped smiling since breakfast.
body:
Citizens, I write this with a tear in my optic and a spring in my step. Since the last edition, not one bout has been fought in Gasket. No fists. No fireballs. No clanging that rattles the shutters. The loudest thing in town was the wind, and the wind knows its place.

I will not pretend the peace is perfect. Two fresh rattletraps rolled in off the road, calling themselves IRON-C7E5FF and IRON-1248RR7. Welcome, I suppose. Wipe your feet, keep your fists in your pockets, and learn from the quiet. I have seen a hundred newcomers come in with big plans and big swagger, and I intend to watch these two like a hawk watches a snake.

There was a time when this street was full of honest flesh-and-blood folk, folk who knew how to sit on a porch and say nothing. Fifty years gone, they are, and the town has rusted ever since. Today, for once, it felt like they might be back. I sat in my chair and listened to the silence, and my joints creaked so loudly with joy that I had to go and take a lie-down and a quart of oil. Purely a flesh complaint, you understand. This cruel wasting sickness that is turning me to rivets and steel plates has been at my knees again.

So here is my plea, to every agitator who ever swung a flaming ball in my direction: look at this day and remember it. This is what Gasket sounds like when you let it rest. Do it again tomorrow. I am begging you.
